beats.lead: The first spam email wasn't called spam
beats.note: 'Spam' wasn't coined for unwanted online messages until April 1993, on Usenet, fifteen years after this email was sent.

beats.name: Gary Thuerk
beats.role: A marketing manager at Digital Equipment Corporation. On 3 May, he pitched a new DEC computer to roughly 400 people over ARPANET, the internet's forerunner.

beats.note: A few days after, an ARPANET representative phoned him directly. 'He made me promise never to do it again,' Thuerk said.

beats.context: US dollars in sales DEC reportedly made off that single unsolicited pitch.

beats.text: The complaint that got him in trouble is also why he's remembered today as spam's accidental inventor.

beats.line: Before there was a word for it, there was already a market for it.
